bug_semantics: An authenticated builder can supply an HTTP(S) target that the Budibase server requests. In the affected REST path, blacklist validation and the network connection resolve the hostname separately; the custom undici dispatcher also overrides the pinned Node agent supplied by fetchWithBlacklist. In the affected OpenAPI-import path, assertUrlIsSafe validates one DNS answer and a later raw node-fetch call resolves again. An attacker-controlled hostname can therefore resolve publicly during validation and to loopback/private space at connect time, producing server-side request forgery.
flaw_origin: The earliest non-refactor origin is 5787dd3f93d67a0e98d6df645a46aa5f6d69328a, which created packages/server/src/integrations/rest.js and passed the builder-controlled datasource URL plus query path directly to node-fetch without connection-time address pinning. Its direct parent has no REST integration file. The later TypeScript rewrite ffc54c37204b69f5b43414c381c694ca91f5d043, blacklist addition 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3, redirect/helper refactors 9273dfb98130a5673a515d8f1708fbeb2fcbe9ce and 7a966383e141001a572f56d419832e32290ef660, and the independent OpenAPI validate-then-fetch instance ba9f7724b342491b8274f2c218494b386bf352a9 preserved or duplicated that underlying unpinned user-URL fetch; they are not the first BIC.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-xg5g-26x8-cvf4 and its API record https://api.github.com/repos/Budibase/budibase/security-advisories/GHSA-xg5g-26x8-cvf4 identify @budibase/server <3.40.0 as affected and 3.40.0 as patched, and document both DNS-rebinding paths. BIC https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/5787dd3f93d67a0e98d6df645a46aa5f6d69328a creates packages/server/src/integrations/rest.js; its read method calls fetch(this.config.url + path, ...), establishing a builder-configured server request without DNS pinning. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 80ebb9a740feb94af7bcdc609b6bd5af3305fc96 packages/server/src/integrations/rest.js` returns no path, directly proving the vulnerable feature absent from the BIC parent; `git merge-base` returns the BIC itself against affected tags 3.39.14 and 3.39.29. History reconstruction shows ffc54c37204b69f5b43414c381c694ca91f5d043 deletes rest.js and adds rest.ts as a rewrite, while 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 adds a pre-fetch blacklist check but leaves the separate fetch resolution. The OpenAPI sibling flaw is introduced by https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/ba9f7724b342491b8274f2c218494b386bf352a9 in packages/server/src/api/controllers/query/import/index.ts; its direct parent f4c9bd1ec6ea2fdae4b2fa8e16a8cabab2f1b8bd has neither assertUrlIsSafe nor the manual-redirect validate/fetch pair. At tag 3.39.14, git tree inspection finds import/index.ts:98/114-115 validating with assertUrlIsSafe then calling raw fetch(currentUrl), rest.ts:772/788/793 installing an undici dispatcher inside the custom fetchWithBlacklist fetchFn, and outboundFetch.ts:55/192 supplying a pinned Node agent that the dispatcher bypasses. Remediation is the two-commit stack 5758bdb242802ca20c4ed0dc579e4330ee898ef3 plus direct/final fix https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/1fecb3fc3497e8db7b60b42cc514ce304ffe3a41: 5758 exports createPinnedLookup and passes pinnedIp to custom fetch functions; 1fec routes OpenAPI import through utils.fetchWithBlacklist and supplies createPinnedLookup(pinnedIp) to the REST dispatcher. Tag 3.39.29 still contains raw fetch(currentUrl) and the unpinned REST setDispatcher call; tag 3.39.30 already contains both fixed forms, so repository tags show an earlier 3.39.30 backport even though the published supported package boundary is 3.40.0. Tag 3.40.0 contains 1fec and shows import/index.ts:100 using utils.fetchWithBlacklist plus rest.ts:750/775 pinning the dispatcher lookup. `git cat-file commit 5787dd3f93d67a0e98d6df645a46aa5f6d69328a` provides the exact human author/committer and trailer-free message quoted in ai_marker. reasoning: Commit-minimality reconciliation 2026-08-29: introducer corrected to ba9f7724 after first-write/ancestry re-verification (see evidence tail). introducer_parent corrected to f4c9bd1e (same recheck). BIC correction 2026-08-29: introducer_sha 5787dd3f93d67a0e98d6df645a46aa5f6d69328a -> ba9f7724 after line-level first-write re-verification (see evidence tail). The attack-enabling dataflow begins when 5787dd3f93d67a0e98d6df645a46aa5f6d69328a first adds a REST datasource that joins builder-controlled URL components and performs the server-side fetch without binding the connection to a validated address. The parent-tree absence makes this the earliest proven BIC. Following the line through the JavaScript-to-TypeScript rewrite and later blacklist/helper changes avoids falsely selecting a move, attempted mitigation, or refactor. Those mitigations checked one DNS result but continued to connect using a fresh resolution; the later OpenAPI importer independently reproduced the same validate-then-fetch error, and the REST undici dispatcher defeated the shared helper's Node-agent pin. The 3.39.14 and 3.39.29 trees exhibit both advisory-described bypasses; 1fecb3fc3497e8db7b60b42cc514ce304ffe3a41, on top of 5758bdb242802ca20c4ed0dc579e4330ee898ef3, removes both by routing OpenAPI through the pinned helper and pinning the actual undici dispatcher lookup. The published 3.40.0 patched boundary contains that direct fix, while repository tag 3.39.30 also contains it. AI attribution is judged only from the selected BIC commit object, which is a human-authored, human-committed, trailer-free commit, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
